title: The iron(III) thiocyanate equilibrium
body: When a solution of iron(III) nitrate is mixed with potassium thiocyanate, a deep red colour appears because of the complex ion [Fe(SCN)]2+. The system reaches the equilibrium Fe3+(aq) + SCN-(aq) <=> [Fe(SCN)]2+(aq), in which Fe3+ is yellow and the complex is deep red, so the intensity of the red colour shows how much complex is present. A student divides the equilibrium mixture into several test tubes to study Le Chatelier's principle. To one she adds more potassium thiocyanate; to another she adds oxalic acid, which reacts with Fe3+ to form the stable complex ion [Fe(C2O4)3]3-; to a third she adds mercury(II) chloride, which reacts with SCN- ions to form stable [Hg(SCN)4]2-. The temperature is kept constant throughout.
